This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).

2. This is a bail application U/S.439 of Cr.P.C. by the Petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Mancheswar P.S.Case No. 426 of 2021 corresponding to C.T. Case No. 6925 of 2021 pending in the file of learned J.M.F.C-II, Bhubaneswar for commission of offence punishable Under Sections 420/120- B/406/294/465/506/34 of IPC, on the allegation of cheating the complainants and misappropriating their money to the tune of Rs. 43,61,682/- in the course of business transaction on the pretext of supplying Amul and Ruchi Gold Oil in low prices.

3. In the course of hearing of the bail application, Mr. D.Nayak, learned Sr. Counsel by filing certified copy of complaint instituted by the sister of the Petitioner against the complainants and copy of bail order passed in ABLAPL No. 3669 of 2023, submits that co-accused who is the father of the present Petitioner and against whom the main allegation of cheating is directed has already been released on bail pursuant to the order passed on 17.05.2023 in ABLAPL No. 3669 of 2023 and the present case is the outcome of the complaint lodged by the sister of the Petitioner.
Mr. D. Nayak also files photo copies of Bank deposits in the name of one of the complainants on various dates which according to the learned Sr. counsel, is for a total sum of Rs. 17,41,250/-.

Learned Sr. counsel also submits that the Petitioner has already deposited the dues of the informant/complainants and there being business transaction disputes among the parties, the Petitioner may kindly be granted bail.
4. On the other hand, Mr. S.R. Roul, ASC, however, strongly opposes the bail application of the Rakesh Kumar Mohanty vs State Of Odisha ...

In addition, Mr. A. Nayak, learned counsel after entering appearance for the Informant by filing Vakalatnama in the Court today opposes the bail application of the Petitioner by inter-alia submitting that the Petitioner and his father had connived and cheated the complainants in this case for a huge amount of more than Rupees 46 Lakhs on the pretext of supplying Amul and Ruchi Gold Oil in low prices in the course of their business transaction and the Petitioner, thereby, should not be granted bail.
5. After having considered the rival submissions made and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of accusations raised against the Petitioner and keeping in view the nature of dispute as well as the complaint lodged by both the parties against each other and regard being had to the pretrial detention of the Petitioner since 20.03.2023 and taking into account the other circumstances on record in entirety including grant of bail to co-accused Rabindra Kumar Mohanty pursuant to an order passed on 17.05.2023 in ABLAPL No. 3669 of 2023 and the allegation against the Petitioner and the co-accused granted with bail being more or less same and the law laid down by the Apex Court in Satendra Kumar Antil Vrs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2021) 10 SCC 773, this Court admits the Petitioner to bail.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vrs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2021) 10 SCC 773
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Hence, the bail application of the Petitioner stands allowed and the Petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two solvent sureties for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the Petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail,
(ii) the Petitioner shall attend the trial Court on each date of posting without fail unless his attendance is dispensed with,
(iii) the Petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till disposal of the case (iv) the Petitioner shall report attendance before the jurisdiction Police Station once in a fortnight preferably on Sunday in between 10 A.M. to 12 Noon for three (03)
months from the actual date of his release from the custody.
The I.I.C. of Jurisdictional Police Station shall not detain the Petitioner unnecessarily after recording his attendance beyond the time as stipulated.

It is clarified that the Court in seisin of the case will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioner without further reference to this Court, if any of the above conditions are violated or a case for cancellation of bail is otherwise made out.

In the wake of aforesaid, the subsequent involvement of the petitioner in future for grave and serious offences on prima facie accusations may be treated as a ground for cancellation of bail in this case.
7. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
